narrative:
On July 28, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,610 cases across 41 judges and heard 1,030 matters, yielding an overall hearing rate of 39.5%. This marks a drop in courtroom efficiency compared to previous benchmark days, falling below the 44.5% hearing rate recorded on July 20 (1,165 of 2,620 heard), 49.2% on July 17 (1,037 of 2,108 heard), and 45.4% on July 10 (926 of 2,038 heard).

Performance highlights across individual court halls demonstrated notable variance in clearance speed. Justice Vijaykumar A. Patil in Court Hall 32 recorded one of the highest conversion rates, hearing 40 out of 53 scheduled cases (75.5%). Justice Suraj Govindaraj maintained consistent efficiency across dual listings, hearing 64 of 110 cases (58.2%) in Hall 10 and 61 of 105 cases (58.1%) in Hall 11. Justice S Vishwajith Shetty addressed the largest single workload of the day in Hall 19, hearing 119 of 321 scheduled matters (37.1%). In contrast, Court Hall 26 under Justice S Rachaiah saw 0 of its 40 listed cases heard.

Analysis by procedural stage indicates that cases listed for Orders achieved the highest progress, with 440 of 920 matters heard (47.8%). Preliminary Hearing (37.3%, 147 of 394 heard) and Admission stages (36.7%, 146 of 398 heard) saw moderate conversion, whereas Final Hearing matters lagged at a 22.2% clearance rate (123 of 555 heard). By subject matter, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the bulk of the docket, with 449 of 1,126 cases heard (39.9%). Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) achieved clearance rates of 44.8% (207 of 462) and 43.4% (119 of 274), respectively, while Regular First Appeals (RFA) recorded lower conversion at 20.0% (31 of 155).
